laws.k: domestic-workers|BR|Complementary Law No. 150 of 2015 on domestic employment
laws.t: Complementary Law No. 150 of 2015 on domestic employment
laws.tp: Equal labor rights: hours, overtime, FGTS, unemployment insurance and social security.
laws.s2: Hak kerja yang setara: jam kerja, lembur, tabungan FGTS, asuransi pengangguran, dan jaminan sosial.

coded.vl: General labor law applies, or a dedicated statute grants its core rights
coded.n: Dedicated law extending general labor rights to domestic workers.

coded.fn: Written contract in a language understood
coded.vl: Written contract required, no language rule
Statutory minimum wage applies on the same terms as other workers
At least monthly payment, documented, with limits on deductions or in-kind pay
coded.n: Monthly payment; deductions for food and housing prohibited.

coded.vl: Normal hours limited as for other workers
coded.n: 8 hours a day, 44 a week, overtime paid.

coded.vl: At least 24 consecutive hours, not replaceable by pay at the employer's request
Equal to or longer than for other workers

coded.fn: Keeping own identity and travel documents
coded.vl: General rule only, not specific to domestic workers or without a penalty
Worker may choose to live out; live-in accommodation must be decent and private
coded.n: Live-in or live-out; housing not deducted.

coded.vl: Worker may change employer without the employer's consent
coded.n: Residence not tied to one employer (Mercosur and humanitarian visas).
Inspection of homes needs consent or scheduling.

coded.vl: Courts or labor tribunals on the same terms as other workers, or fee-free
Included in the general social security system, including maternity

coded.fn: Protection from abuse, harassment and violence
coded.vl: General criminal or civil law only
May form and join trade unions

dec.n: Workers of the Hacienda Brasil Verde v. Brazil
dec.pe: Men recruited from poor regions of Brazil were taken to a remote ranch and kept working by debt and threats. It was the Inter-American Court’s first judgment on slavery, and it found Brazil responsible.
dec.pi: Pria yang direkrut dari wilayah miskin Brasil dibawa ke peternakan terpencil dan dipaksa bekerja dengan utang dan ancaman. Ini putusan pertama Mahkamah Inter-Amerika tentang perbudakan, dan Brasil dinyatakan bertanggung jawab.

dec.pe: An Italian woman who had lived in Brazil for decades was refused the old-age benefit because she was not Brazilian. The Supreme Court said residents are entitled to it like citizens.
dec.pi: Seorang perempuan Italia yang sudah puluhan tahun tinggal di Brasil ditolak tunjangan lansia karena bukan warga Brasil. MA Federal menyatakan penduduk berhak seperti warga negara.

dec.n: The “dirty list” of employers using slave labour (ADPF 509)
dec.pe: Brazil publishes the names of employers found using slave-like labour, including of migrant workers in garment workshops. An employers’ association challenged the list, and the Supreme Court upheld it.
dec.pi: Brasil menerbitkan nama majikan yang terbukti memakai kerja mirip perbudakan, termasuk pekerja migran di bengkel garmen. Asosiasi pengusaha menggugat daftar itu, dan MA Federal mempertahankannya.
